stories.headline: Naver and Nvidia team up to build gigawatt-scale AI factory, starting at 55MW in 2027

key_facts.fact: Nvidia and Naver announced on June 7, 2026 that Naver will expand sovereign AI infrastructure starting at 55 megawatts with plans to move to gigawatt scale using the Nvidia DSX platform
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA and NAVER today announced that NAVER will expand sovereign AI infrastructure, starting at 55 megawatts with plans to move to gigawatt scale using the NVIDIA DSX platform to rapidly design, build and scale full-stack, end-to-end AI platforms that can serve enterprises, industries and government.

key_facts.fact: The new DSX-powered cloud will expand Naver's Gak Sejong data center in Sejong, South Korea, which will serve as a forward base
key_facts.excerpt: The new DSX-powered cloud will expand NAVER's GAK Sejong data center, a next-generation, hyperscale facility in Sejong, South Korea, built to power the company's rapidly growing AI and cloud services.

key_facts.fact: Naver plans to begin with 55MW operation in the first half of 2027, expand overseas infrastructure to 100MW within the same year, and to 200MW by 2028
key_facts.excerpt: Starting with 55MW operation in the first half of 2027, the company plans to expand its infrastructure to 100MW within the same year and to 200MW overseas by 2028.

key_facts.fact: One gigawatt is roughly four times the maximum capacity of Naver's largest domestic data center, Gak Sejong, and can accommodate hundreds of thousands of Nvidia's latest GPUs simultaneously
key_facts.excerpt: One gigawatt is nearly fourfold the maximum data capacity of Naver's Gak Sejong center and is capable of accommodating hundreds of thousands of Nvidia's latest GPU, according to the company.

key_facts.fact: Naver Chairman Lee Hae-jin and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met at Naver's 1784 headquarters in Seongnam to discuss a roadmap to expand into Europe and the Middle East beyond Asia-Pacific
key_facts.excerpt: The two companies have already agreed on the direction of expanding their AI infrastructure ecosystem business beyond the Asia-Pacific region into Europe and the Middle East.

stories.headline: Nvidia and SK Hynix sign multi-year pact for next-gen memory across Vera Rubin and Jetson Thor

key_facts.fact: Nvidia and SK Hynix announced on June 7, 2026 a multi-year technology partnership to advance next-generation memory for the global AI factory buildout and accelerate semiconductor design and manufacturing
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA and SK hynix today announced a multiyear technology partnership to advance next-generation memory for the global AI factory buildout and accelerate semiconductor design and manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix will co-develop memory for Nvidia Vera Rubin AI supercomputers, Vera CPUs, RTX Spark-powered PCs and Jetson Thor robotic computing platforms
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix will diversify into new markets NVIDIA is creating — across AI infrastructure, personal AI and physical AI — codeveloping memory for NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI supercomputers, Vera CPUs, RTX Spark-powered PCs and Jetson Thor robotic computing platforms.

key_facts.fact: Industry analysts estimate SK Hynix holds roughly 60% to 70% of HBM4 volume allocated to Vera Rubin, with Samsung at approximately 25% to 30% and Micron supplying the remainder
key_facts.excerpt: Industry analysts estimate SK Hynix holds roughly 60% to 70% of HBM4 volume allocated to Vera Rubin, with Samsung at approximately 25% to 30% and Micron supplying the remainder.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said 'AI factories are the engines of the next industrial revolution, and advanced memory is essential to their performance'
key_facts.excerpt: AI factories are the engines of the [next industrial revolution], and advanced memory is essential to their performance, said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA.

key_facts.fact: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said SK Hynix and Nvidia 'have laid the groundwork for this over several years, and this partnership is the result that shows the depth of cooperation between the two companies'
key_facts.excerpt: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said, SK Hynix and Nvidia have laid the groundwork for this over several years, and this partnership is the result that shows the depth of cooperation between the two companies.

stories.headline: LG expands Nvidia pact to cover physical AI, cooling and 800V DC power for AI data centers

key_facts.fact: LG Group Chairman Koo Kwang-mo and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met on June 8, 2026 at LG Twin Towers in Yeouido, Seoul to expand strategic cooperation across physical AI, AI data centers and mobility
key_facts.excerpt: LG and NVIDIA will expand strategic cooperation across next-generation AI-driven industries, including Physical AI, AI data centers and mobility, to jointly shape the future industrial landscape. The two companies held a top executives meeting on the 8th at LG Twin Tower in Yeouido, Seoul.

key_facts.fact: LG Electronics will pursue certification cooperation on Coolant Distribution Units (CDU) and cold plates for AI data centers, plus modular data center design based on Nvidia's Digital Twin Supercomputing Matrix (DSX)
key_facts.excerpt: LG Electronics will proceed with certification cooperation for cooling solutions such as Coolant Distribution Units (CDU) and cold plates for AI data centers, and will also collaborate on modular data center design technology based on NVIDIA's Digital Twin Supercomputing Matrix (DSX).

key_facts.fact: LG Energy Solution is discussing an 800V direct current-based power solution and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) cooperation with Nvidia to handle AI data centers' rising power demand
key_facts.excerpt: LG Energy Solution is discussing an 800V direct current (DC)-based power solution cooperation plan with NVIDIA to respond to the increasing power demand of AI data centers.

key_facts.fact: Huang said today's data centers already reach hundreds of megawatts and future ultra-large blocks will require advanced cooling and power supply technologies where LG has 'fantastic capabilities'
key_facts.excerpt: Today's data centers are already massive, reaching hundreds of megawatts (MW), but future ultra-large-scale data center blocks will require cutting-edge technologies such as advanced cooling and power supply. He continued, LG has fantastic capabilities in this field, and we are working together on future architecture design.

key_facts.fact: LG Uplus will build a large AI data center using Nvidia GPUs and LG CNS is developing scalable AI factory infrastructure using Nvidia's reference architecture
key_facts.excerpt: LG Uplus is going to establish a large AI data centre using the NVIDIA GPUs, and LG CNS is developing scalable AI factory infrastructure using NVIDIA's reference architecture. Additionally, LG Energy Solution is developing future power technologies, such as the 800-volt direct current power technology, which has been demanded by the future AI data centre.

stories.headline: Hyundai pitches Nvidia on $5.9B Saemangeum AI valley while expanding mobility and robotics ties

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung on June 8, 2026 at the automaker's headquarters in Seoul to discuss expanding partnership across mobility, robotics and AI factories
key_facts.excerpt: I am very excited to partner with Hyundai across all areas of AI, from mobility to robotics and AI factories, Nvidia Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jensen Huang told reporters after a meeting with Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung at the automaker's headquarters in southern Seoul.

key_facts.fact: Chung briefed Huang on a 9 trillion-won (US$5.87 billion) project announced in February to transform 1.12 million square meters of the Saemangeum reclaimed land area into an AI, robotics and hydrogen hub
key_facts.excerpt: The 9 trillion-won (US$5.87 billion) project, announced in February, calls for developing 1.12 million square meters of land in the Saemangeum area. The plan includes construction of an AI data center, a robotics manufacturing and components cluster, a water electrolysis plant and solar power facilities, among other projects.

key_facts.fact: Huang said 'the next wave of AI is mobility and physical AI. This is the future where AI understands the world and can come out and do good work, productive work for the world. This is the time for Hyundai'
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are uniting AI and Hyundai's expertise in mobility to transform the future of mobility and the future of robotics, Huang said. The next wave of AI is mobility and physical AI. This is the future where AI understands the world and can come out and do good work, productive work for the world. This is the time for Hyundai.

key_facts.fact: The two companies are jointly investing roughly $3 billion to establish an Nvidia AI Technology Center and a Hyundai Motor Group Physical AI Application Center in Korea
key_facts.excerpt: The two are also supporting Korea's physical AI initiative. Together with the Science Ministry, they agreed to invest roughly $3 billion to establish an Nvidia AI Technology Center and a Hyundai Motor Group Physical AI Application Center in Korea.

key_facts.fact: Hyundai previously unveiled plans to build an AI factory powered by 50,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs for in-vehicle AI, autonomous driving, smart manufacturing and robotics
key_facts.excerpt: Hyundai unveiled plans to build an AI factory powered by 50,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs to train, validate and deploy AI models for in-vehicle AI, autonomous driving, smart manufacturing and robotics.

stories.headline: Doosan opens Nvidia partnership to SMRs, gas turbines and an Agentic Robot OS

key_facts.fact: Doosan Group said on June 8, 2026 that four affiliates — Doosan Robotics, Doosan Bobcat, Doosan Enerbility and Doosan Corporation Electro-Materials BG — will expand cooperation with Nvidia across physical AI, robotics and AI factory infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia and South Korea's Doosan Group announced they will expand their partnership across physical AI, robotics and AI factory infrastructure, the latest in a string of deals struck during CEO Jensen Huang's visit to Seoul. The collaboration spans four Doosan units — Doosan Robotics, Doosan Bobcat, Doosan Enerbility and Doosan Corporation Electro-Materials BG.

key_facts.fact: Doosan Enerbility is exploring how its gas turbines, steam turbines and small modular reactors plus Doosan Fuel Cell's hydrogen fuel-cell systems can support Nvidia's DSX AI factory platform
key_facts.excerpt: Doosan Enerbility is exploring opportunities to support NVIDIA AI factories and the NVIDIA DSX AI factory platform through its large-scale power infrastructure portfolio, including gas turbines, steam turbines and small modular reactors, together with Doosan Fuel Cell's hydrogen fuel-cell systems.

key_facts.fact: Doosan Robotics is integrating Nvidia Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, the Cosmos world foundation models, Newton physics engine and Jetson Thor into its Agentic Robot OS — an AI platform connecting perception, reasoning, simulation, learning and on-device inference
key_facts.excerpt: Doosan Robotics is integrating NVIDIA Isaac Sim and NVIDIA Isaac Lab open robotics frameworks, NVIDIA Cosmos open world foundation models, the open source Newton physics engine and NVIDIA Jetson Thor to advance its Agentic Robot OS — an AI-powered platform connecting perception, reasoning, simulation, learning and on-device inference.

key_facts.fact: Doosan Robotics also plans to develop reference use cases for industrial tasks such as pallet sorting and polishing and to extend to dual-arm and humanoid form factors
key_facts.excerpt: It also plans to develop reference use cases for tasks specialised for industrial sites, such as pallet sorting and polishing work, as well as new forms such as dual-arm and humanoid robots.

key_facts.fact: Huang said combining Nvidia DSX and physical AI with Doosan's energy, robotics and advanced materials businesses can secure new growth engines in intelligent robots, autonomous industrial equipment and next-generation infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: By combining Nvidia DSX and physical AI with Doosan's energy, Robotics, and advanced materials businesses, Doosan Group can secure new growth engines in key AI-era fields such as intelligent robots, autonomous industrial equipment, and next-generation infrastructure.

stories.headline: Industrial AI startup PhysicsX raises $300M Series C at $2.4B led by Temasek

key_facts.fact: London-based PhysicsX raised $300 million in a Series C led by Singapore sovereign wealth fund Temasek at a valuation of roughly $2.4 billion, more than doubling the ~$1 billion valuation from its previous round 12 months earlier
key_facts.excerpt: PhysicsX, a British startup that develops artificial intelligence models for manufacturing components like jet engines and semiconductors, has raised US$300 million at a valuation of roughly US$2.4 billion... The company was valued at almost US$1 billion at its last funding round.

key_facts.fact: New investors Intrepid Growth Partners and M&G Catalyst joined existing backers including Nvidia, Applied Materials, Atomico, General Catalyst, July Fund, NGP, Radius and Siemens
key_facts.excerpt: The round is led by Temasek, with participation from new investors M&G Investments and Intrepid Growth Partners, alongside existing investors including Applied Materials, Atomico, General Catalyst, July Fund, NGP, NVIDIA, Radius, and Siemens.

key_facts.fact: PhysicsX builds AI models that replace traditional engineering simulations, predicting physical behavior in seconds instead of hours or days; customers include Applied Materials, Siemens and Stellantis
key_facts.excerpt: PhysicsX focuses on software that lets aerospace and automotive firms design, test and assemble parts. The company provides an AI model that predicts how physical objects behave, which it says makes the process much faster than conventional simulation software for engineering... Customers include Applied Materials, Siemens and Stellantis.

key_facts.fact: CEO Jacomo Corbo said revenue will be 'close to US$50 million' for the year and the company aims to more than double the figure in 2027 while expanding to a roughly six-month customer backlog
key_facts.excerpt: Corbo said revenue will be close to US$50 million for the year and the company aims to more than double the figure in 2027... The startup, which last raised funds 12 months ago, needs more cash to expand its staff in part because of a roughly six-month backlog of customer demand.

key_facts.fact: PhysicsX has grown headcount from 150 to 350 over the past year and will fund US expansion plus a new Singapore office
key_facts.excerpt: PhysicsX has grown from 150 to 350 employees over the past year and more than quadrupled revenue over the past two years... The Series C will fund expansion in the US and a new office in Singapore, Temasek's home market.

stories.headline: Memory vendors say China's CXMT DDR5 is no bargain — prices match Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron

key_facts.fact: Memory module vendors at Computex 2026 told Wccftech that CXMT's DDR5 prices are 'almost on par' with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, debunking the assumption that the Chinese newcomer would crash consumer pricing
key_facts.excerpt: Multiple suppliers revealed that CXMT's memory is not cheap — its DDR5 solution pricing is virtually on par with Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron. CXMT's primary advantage is not price disruption but rather its relatively ample traditional DRAM production capacity.

key_facts.fact: CXMT's edge comes from supply, not price: since it does not prioritize HBM or SOCAMM for AI customers it has more traditional DRAM capacity available for client markets
key_facts.excerpt: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is gaining attention as a potential new force in the global DRAM market, but memory module vendors say the Chinese chipmaker is not offering the low-cost DDR5 supply many in the PC sector had hoped for.

key_facts.fact: CXMT also does not impose the supply penalties that Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron currently force on customers seeking additional allocation — making it an attractive secondary source despite matching prices
key_facts.excerpt: Multiple suppliers revealed that CXMT's memory is not cheap... CXMT's primary advantage is not price disruption but rather its relatively ample traditional DRAM production capacity. Since CXMT has not prioritized capacity allocation for AI customers, nor has it aggressively pursued advanced solutions such as HBM or SOCAMM, it has been able to maintain a foothold in the traditional DRAM supply market.

key_facts.fact: A Lexar regional manager warned at Computex that DRAM prices could double by year-end, with current channel discounts merely reflecting short-term inventory clearance
key_facts.excerpt: A Lexar regional manager warned at COMPUTEX that DRAM prices could double by year-end, with current channel discounts merely reflecting short-term inventory clearance.
